header:
Date: 2026-05-04
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Rachel Gomez (HearthBank VP Legal), Tom Alvarez (HearthBank CISO), Priya Singh (HearthBank Head of Procurement)
Meeting link: zoom.us/j/xxxxxxxxxx
summary: Procurement and legal review of Redwood's MSA/DPA/SLA and onboarding requirements. Customer is focused on data residency, encryption/KMS, SOC 2/ISO evidence, and SLA/penalty language for 99th percentile latency. Redwood AE/SE discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment, onboarding timeline and pricing options. Agreed next steps: send redlines, security docs, schedule technical benchmark.
topics: MSA redlines; DPA terms (data retention, deletion); SLAs (99th pctl latency, uptime); KMS/HSM and key ownership; Private deployment/VPC options; Pricing and committed capacity; Onboarding timeline and benchmarks
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll do a quick agenda. We're here to walk through the MSA and DPA and chat SLAs and onboarding requirements.
[00:08] Rachel Gomez: Thanks Maya. We got the files, we did a quick pass — a few legal flags, mainly around data residency, breach notification, and indemnity.
[00:17] Tom Alvarez: Hi, I'm Tom, CISO. My team dug into encryption, KMS integration, and audit logs. A lot of our questions are around key management and whether Redwood has HSM integration or customer-managed keys.
[00:29] Liam Chen: hi Tom, yes we support customer-managed keys via K M S integrations and have options for HSM for private deployments. The private control plane supports bringing your own key material — there are docs i'll share.
[00:40] Priya Singh: timeline wise, procurement wants to understand pricing for committed capacity and what the SLA tiers look like, and also onboarding duration for Dedicated or Private.
[00:49] Maya Patel: For pricing we have usage-based hosted plus reserved capacity options for Dedicated. I'll put together committed monthly tiers and the breakouts. For onboarding Dedicated is usually 2-4 weeks depending on network and approvals; Private on-prem can take longer, 6-10 weeks typically.
[01:05] Rachel Gomez: On the DPA, our legal team wants specific deletion timelines and proof of deletion. Also we want subprocessor lists.
[01:14] Liam Chen: we can provide subprocessor list and addendum language; deletion proofs are usually audit logs and purge reports, we can provide those for contract. Small note — sometimes our auto-transcripts spell K V cache oddly, but we do have prefix/KV cache logs if you need them.
[01:28] Tom Alvarez: SLA: we need 99th percentile latency SLOs for generation endpoints and a financial credit in case of breach. Can you commit to numbers with Dedicated?
[01:38] Maya Patel: For Dedicated we have SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. Typical 99th pctl depends on model and seq len; we can commit to a Dedicated SLO of X ms for specific models in the contract, and we include fallback policies to keep apps online. We'll need to scope which model family you intend to use for the exact numbers.
[01:53] Priya Singh: Is there an option to route certain requests to hosted if dedicated capacity is saturated? We want graceful degradation.
[02:03] Liam Chen: yes, smart routing is supported. Policy-based routing can route by latency or cost and fall back to compatible model variants in another region or tier. There might be slight variance in token cost when routing to hosted.
[02:15] Rachel Gomez: Liability caps — we prefer to keep them higher than standard; how flexible is Redwood on liability and indemnity?
[02:22] Maya Patel: We can discuss commercial terms; usually liability caps are tiered with contract size and enterprise packages. I'll flag legal for escalation if you have specific redlines.
[02:30] Tom Alvarez: Security questionnaires — we have a vendor questionnaire. Can you share SOC2 and ISO attestation and any penetration test reports? Also, how are logs retained and can we get audit trails per tenant?
[02:44] Liam Chen: we will share SOC 2 Type II report and ISO summary, plus penetration test summaries. Logs retention is configurable; the console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns, and we can export audit logs for your security team.
[02:58] Priya Singh: Procurement wants confirmation on data residency: our production data must reside in us-east-1 and only processed within the US. Is that doable?
[03:07] Maya Patel: For hosted we have region controls and can pin requests to regions; for strict residency we recommend Dedicated in a US region or Private deployment. We'll document the flow and provide attestation language.
[03:18] Rachel Gomez: DPA language about subprocessors and cross-border transfer — we need EU standard contractual clauses if any data crosses borders.
[03:25] Liam Chen: we'll include SCP/ SCC language where applicable and list subprocessors with locations.
[03:31] Tom Alvarez: A few technical asks: 1) can you run a benchmark with our prompt set to show median and 99th latency using your prefix/KV cache and batching? 2) For private deployment, can we see network diagrams and what network ACLs are required?
[03:46] Liam Chen: absolutely. We can run a benchmark — preferably an SE-led run with your sample prompts; we'll capture tail latency. For private we'll share network diagrams and required open ports and firewall rules.
[03:56] Maya Patel: Good — let's capture next steps: I'll send pricing and redlined MSA/DPA by Friday; Liam will send security docs and schedule the benchmark; Priya will confirm procurement timeline and get back on vendor questionnaire items.
[04:09] Priya Singh: Sounds good. One more question — if we start with Hosted for speed but later move to Dedicated, is data migration straightforward?
[04:18] Liam Chen: yes, we support model version pinning and offer migration paths. There are export/import and snapshot mechanisms for KV caches and prompt sets; we'll outline the process.
[04:29] Rachel Gomez: For the SLA credits, can you provide sample language? Our legal prefers a clear formula tied to downtime minutes.
[04:36] Maya Patel: We'll include sample SLA and credit calculation language in the redline packet.
[04:41] Tom Alvarez: Regarding KMS, do you allow BYOK where keys never leave our control?
[04:46] Liam Chen: in Private and some Dedicated configs yes — BYOK is supported via KMS integrations and HSM for on-prem. For hosted we offer managed keys or customer-managed keys depending on contract.
[04:58] Rachel Gomez: Ok we'll review and get redlines back by next week. Thanks everyone.
[05:03] Maya Patel: Thanks all — we'll follow up with docs and next steps.
[05:07] (meeting ends)
